players.note: Not only is Kaelon Black the single most indispensable handcuff RB in fantasy football, but Black has been offering some stand-alone value lately. In Week 8, Black had 12-63-1 rushing against the Falcons. In Week 9, he had 11-70-0 rushing vs. the Raiders. On Sunday, Black had 11-53-1 rushing and 2-13-0 receiving against the Cowboys. 49ers head coach Mike Shanahan seems to be making an earnest effort to avoid overworking lead back Christian McCaffrey, which has meant a healthy dose of carries for Black, a third-round rookie from Indiana. Black is averaging 4.5 yards per carry, and his rushing success rate is north of 57%, well above league average. If you're a McCaffrey stakeholder who hasn't rostered Black yet, this would be a good week to fix that. Even if you don't have McCaffrey, if Black is just sitting there on waivers in your league, he's probably worth a roster spot. If McCaffrey were to go down, Black would instantly become one of the more valuable running backs in fantasy.

First-round rookie Makai Lemon has had six receptions in each of the Eagles' last two games, but his uptick in usage has come while WRs DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks have been out with injuries. There's a good chance the Eagles get Smith and Wicks back this week. With the Eagles now on their third different starting QB this season (Joe Milton), there's just not enough passing-game juice to make multiple Eagles receivers fantasy-relevant, and Smith is clearly the No. 1 receiver in Philadelphia.

The Buccaneers are the run-heaviest team in the NFL, running the ball on 52.4% of their offensive snaps. Bucky Irving is Tampa Bay's undisputed No. 1 running back, but Kenny Gainwell is one of the better backups in the league and a priority handcuff. Gainwell has 63-305-0 rushing this season and is averaging 4.8 yards per carry, but there have been only two games this season in which he's had more than five carries. Gainwell offers no stand-alone value.

Ryan Flournoy might work better as a No. 3 receiver than as a No. 2 receiver. With George Pickens sidelined by a hamstring injury in Week 9, Flournoy seemed poised for a big game against the Colts, but he finished with 2-53-0 on only three targets. Pickens returned to action in Week 10, so Flournoy was back in the role of No. 3 behind Pickens and CeeDee Lamb. Flournoy had 6-71-1 on seven targets vs. the 49ers. Flournoy has a terrific Week 11 matchup against a Titans defense that has given up the most fantasy points to wide receivers. Then he has an appealing Week 12 matchup against the Eagles, who have also been generous to receivers in 2026.

Before you consider placing a claim on Chig Okonkwo this week, check his injury status. Okonkwo left the Commanders' Week 10 win over the Giants with a back injury but returned later in the game. Okonkwo has an extremely favorable schedule coming up and could be a multi-week solution for fantasy gamers who have been streaming the TE position. This week, Okonkwo faces the Bengals, who entered Week 10 having allowed the second-most receiving yards per game and ninth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends. In Week 11, Okonkwo gets a Cardinals defense that has allowed the eighth-most fantasy points per game to TEs. Okonkwo has 27-263-0 on 39 targets this season. Those are modest numbers, but he's becoming a more prominent target earner with WR Terry McLaurin out for the rest of the season with a torn patellar tendon. Okonkwo has drawn seven or more targets in three of his last four games.

It would be nice if Antonio Williams were getting more target volume. In the three games the Commanders have played since WR Terry McLaurin went down with a season-ending knee injury, Williams has 10-121-1 on 15 targets. The third-round rookie from Clemson had a 31-yard TD catch against the Giants last week, but he was targeted only twice. Williams' target share since the McLaurin injury is 15.5%. Perhaps Williams' target share and efficiency will increase as he adjusts to life in the NFL. Williams is averaging a modest 1.44 yards per route run. Williams' upcoming schedule is promising. In Week 11, he faces the Bengals, whose high-powered offense is capable of forcing QB Jayden Daniels and the Commanders into a pass-heavy game script. Williams faces a mediocre Cardinals defense in Week 12, and in Week 13 he gets a Titans pass defense that entered Week 10 having allowed the most fantasy points per game to wide receivers. Williams is playable in any of the next three weeks and can also provide useful WR depth.

It was reasonable to worry that the fantasy value of rookie WR Caleb Douglas could be obliterated by an injury to Dolphins QB Malik Willis. It's not as if Willis has been some sort of fantasy rainmaker, but his backup, Kyle McCord, had never thrown a pass in a regular-season NFL game before Week 11. Despite McCord's inexperience, Douglas had a solid performance on Sunday, with 3-71-0 on a team-high eight targets. Douglas had a 24.2% target share on Sunday and accounted for 33.0% of Miami's receiving yardage. Douglas looks like he could eventually be special. The 6-4, 205-pound Douglas uses his big body to box out defenders and excels in contested-catch situations. He has vise grips for hands. Even if you don't need to use Douglas this week, consider grabbing him for the stretch run. Douglas looks like a star in the making.

Dylan Sampson has played more snaps than starting RB Quinshon Judkins in each of the Browns' last three games, but the two RBs' roles are pretty clearly defined. Judkins is Cleveland's early-down back, Sampson the passing-down back. In the four games he's played since returning from a knee injury, Sampson is averaging only 4.8 carries a game, but he's averaging 5.5 targets, 4.0 catches and 38.0 receiving yards per game over that span. The Browns are on bye this week, but Sampson can provide some low-level PPR value and useful depth upon his return.

Mike Gesicki doesn't offer a sturdy floor. He's had 11 or fewer receiving yards in four of his last five games. What Gesicki does offer is touchdown potential. He's caught six TD passes this season, and while Gesicki has gone two consecutive games without scoring a touchdown, he had a touchdown in five straight games from Week 3 to Week 8. Gesicki is attached to red-hot Bengals QB Joe Burrow, who's thrown 20 TD passes in his last five starts. This week, Burrow faces a Washington defense that has allowed the second-most fantasy points to tight ends. Giants TE Isaiah Likely torched the Commanders for 9-127-1 in Week 10.

Omar Cooper Jr. left the Jets' Week 11 loss to the Bills with an ankle injury. If Cooper has a high-ankle sprain, he's going to miss a few weeks, and in his absence, Adonai Mitchell would be the Jets' No. 2 receiver behind No. 1 Garrett Wilson. Sunday against the Bills, Mitchell had 3-59-0 on eight targets. Mitchell has a boom-or-bust profile. He had a 7-142-1 game against the Raiders earlier this month, but Mitchell has also had two zero-catch games this season. He's big (6-2, 205) and fast (he ran a 4.34 at the combine), but Mitchell isn't the most precise route runner, and he sometimes has focus/drop issues. With Cooper's expected absence enhancing Mitchell's short-term target outlook, Mitchell will be playable in matchups against the Chargers and Dolphins the next two weeks.

With Brock Bowers dealing with an ankle injury that could potentially cost him one or more games, and with the Raiders devoid of impactful wide receivers, TE Michael Mayer's short-term target outlook has brightened. Mayer has 41-404-1 on 49 targets. Mayer has more receptions this season than any of the Las Vegas wideouts. This week, Mayer has a matchup against a Denver defense that has been a TE funnel. The Broncos have allowed the third-fewest fantasy points per game to wide receivers, but they've allowed the fourth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends. Rookie QB Fernando Mendoza might lean heavily on Mayer this week.

It's possible (but not likely) that Emari Demercado will be the Texans' lead RB when they host the Colts this week. Woody Marks left the Texans' Week 10 loss to the Browns with a concussion. David Montgomery has missed the last four games with a groin injury, although he returned to practice last week. Demercado played 22 snaps in Week 10 and had 7-16-0 rushing and one catch for -1 yard. It seems as if Montgomery will be back this week. He practiced in full last Friday, but the Texans chose not to activate him for their Week 10 game against the Browns. Marks has little chance to clear concussion protocol before the Texans' Thursday-night game. If Demercado has a significant role in Week 11, he could be playable in an ultra-favorable matchup against the Colts, who went into Week 10 with a run defense that ranked 31st in DVOA and 32nd in EPA per rush.

Darren Waller is streaky, but he's a prolific touchdown scorer for a tight end and provides more than his fair share of big games. Waller has four touchdowns this season, and he's had 50 or more receiving yards in three of his nine games this season. For the season, he has 25-323-4 on 38 targets. Waller sits just outside TE1 range in fantasy scoring with 7.6 half-point PPR points per game. With so many tight ends on bye this week, Waller is a reasonable Week 11 option in a neutral matchup against the Ravens.

Second-year Broncos WR Pat Bryant has been coming on strong and could potentially supplant Courtland Sutton as Denver's No. 2 receiver. Over his last three games, Bryant has 9-147-2 on 10 targets. He's averaged 14.7 yards per target and 2.04 yards per route run this season. The 6-2, 204-pound Bryant has ordinary speed, but he's an advanced route runner with outstanding ball skills. The Broncos' passing game is limited with QB Bo Nix at the helm, but Bryant could be playable this week for WR-needy fantasy teams against the struggling Raiders defense. This is an intriguing young player with the potential to come on quickly.

Well, well, well. It turns out Seth McGowan might have fantasy value after all, even though a Jonathan Taylor trade never came to fruition. We touted McGowan as a potential waiver pickup last week, since it seemed as if the Colts were destined to trade Taylor to one of the half-dozen or so teams rumored to be interested in his services. But there was no deal by last Tuesday's trade deadline, so interest in McGowan as a waiver claim fizzled. Against the Dolphins in Week 10, Taylor played 40 snaps, McGowan 17. But McGowan got carries on 12 of those 17 snaps and finished with 77 rushing yards and a touchdown. It's possible that going forward, the Colts use Taylor and McGowan in much the same way the Rams use Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Williams typically plays a lot more snaps than Corum, but Corum has been getting either a carry or a target on more than half of his snaps. The Colts were run-heavy in their win over the Dolphins on Sunday, running the ball on 60.7% of their offensive snaps. The 3-7 Colts will not have the luxury of run-friendly game scripts very often, but they're likely to be fairly run-heavy anyway, since they're better at running the ball than throwing it, and since the Colts now have one of the worst WR collections in the league after trading away Keenan Allen and Josh Downs at the deadline. In a waiver week where there's very little of interest at the RB position, McGowan might be worth a bid if you need to patch a hole at the position.
Although he offers no stand-alone value, Samaje Perine is a premium handcuff as the backup to Chase Brown in Cincinnati. The Bengals have one of the best offenses in the league.

Chris Rodriguez Jr. mostly offers handcuff value to Bhayshul Tuten stakeholders, but C-Rod could have some low-level stand-alone value in the coming weeks. Rodriguez has 59-233-4 rushing this season. He's had touchdown runs in two of his last three games and four of his last seven. He offers little as a pass-catcher, with just 4-36-0 receiving in 2026. This week, the Jaguars face the Giants, whose run defense ranked 16th in defense-adjusted value over average (DVOA) and 25th in expected points added (EPA) per rush going into Week 10. Then, the Jaguars face the Titans, whose run defense ranked 29th in DVOA and 16th in EPA per rush entering Week 10. Rodriguez might be able to do some damage against those defenses even on limited carries. Because he's such a zero as a pass-catcher, Rodriguez is more appealing in standard-scoring or half-point PPR leagues than in full-point PPR leagues.

In last week's article, we suggested that despite Tank Dell's 100-yard game in Week 9, Xavier Hutchinson was the better Houston receiver to target on waivers because he plays more snaps and runs more routes than Dell. Hutchinson had 4-58-1 on nine targets against the Browns in Week 10. Dell had 3-21-0 on four targets. Hutchinson had a 76.1% snap share on Sunday and ran 33 routes. Dell had a 49.3% snap share and ran 23 routes. Dell is now rostered in more than half of Yahoo leagues, while Hutchinson is available in 97% of them. Hutchinson has lined up in the slot on more than half of his snaps this season. The Texans have a Week 11 matchup with the Colts, who entered Week 10 having allowed the fifth-most fantasy points per game to slot receivers. In a week with so many receivers on bye, Hutchinson is startable in a plus matchup.

If Carnell Tate misses a third straight game with a shoulder injury � and perhaps even if Tate returns to action this week � Elic Ayomanor might be playable in a terrific matchup against the Cowboys. Entering Week 10, Dallas had allowed the seventh-most receiving yards to wide receivers. The Cowboys have given up an average of 34 points over their last three games.

We know our readers are too savvy to chase Jaguars rookie WR Josh Cameron based on his 3-67-1 performance against the Titans in Week 10. But just in case we're wrong about that, here's a reminder not to add Cameron.
